days.summary: Overnight into October 1–2, Russian drones struck Kyiv multiple times, hitting a school and warehouse facilities in Solomianskyi district, residential high-rises in Podilskyi, Obolonskyi and Darnytskyi districts, the Pivdennyi Bridge (hit twice, including while a metro train crossed it), and causing debris damage and fires in open areas across Pecherskyi, Sviatoshynskyi, Dniprovskyi and Holosiivskyi districts.

audit_examples.explanation: c6 describes drone debris found on 'відкритій території' (open ground) in Pecherskyi district with effect 'debris' and target 'open_area', while c7 describes a direct drone strike on a 'non-residential complex' with effect 'direct_hit' and target 'other'. These are described as physically distinct kinds of locations (open ground vs. a non-residential complex/building) with no shared address or explicit statement that they are the same spot. The Kyiv Post wording 'another drone struck a non-residential complex' signals a separate incident, not a restatement of the debris-on-open-ground report. The site's single target field ('open_area') also doesn't match c7's own target ('other'), confirming these were merged despite describing different places/incidents.

days.summary: On the night and day of 2 October 2026, Russian strikes on Kyiv repeatedly hit the Pivdennyi Bridge, caused a drone strike on a residential high-rise in Darnytskyi district, blast damage to a residential building, two non-residential buildings, a medical facility and a vehicle in Holosiivskyi district, debris and fire in Podilskyi district, and the Pivnichnyy (Northern) Bridge was hit the following morning.

audit_examples.explanation: All four claims come from the exact same Suspilne Kyiv report filed at 10:41 about Holosiivskyi district, with no distinct addresses given, and are phrased as a list of consequences from a single strike: "в одному з житлових будинків пошкоджено перекриття паркінгу" (c3), "вибито вікна та пошкоджено фасади двох нежитлових будівель" (c4), "в одній із медичних установ вибито 5 вікон" (c5), and "пошкоджено автомобіль" (c6). The repeated 'в одному з...'/'в одній із...' construction indicates these are all secondary/blast-damage effects (parking floor, nearby non-residential buildings, a medical facility's windows, a car) radiating from one impact point in Holosiivskyi district reported together, not four separate strikes. Splitting them into four independent sites double-counts what is almost certainly a single strike's blast damage as four separate impact sites.

Site 3 merges four claims describing different kinds of buildings/objects in Holosiivskyi district with no address linking them: a residential building's parking floor ('в одному з житлових будинків пошкоджено перекриття паркінгу', c3), two separate non-residential buildings ('вибито вікна та пошкоджено фасади двох нежитлових будівель', c4), a medical facility ('в одній із медичних установ вибито 5 вікон', c5), and a vehicle ('пошкоджено автомобіль', c6). The summary itself admits there is no distinct address evidence ('with no distinct addresses') and only infers via the shared report timestamp that these are 'secondary effects radiating from one impact point.' That is a speculative leap: a single Suspilne roundup commonly aggregates damage from multiple separate hits/incidents across a district, not necessarily one strike. Different building types (residential, non-residential x2, medical) with no confirmed shared location should not be presented as one site without stronger evidence.

The site's target field is set to 'residential_highrise', but only c3 concerns a residential building (and only its parking floor). The other claims in the same site describe two non-residential/office buildings (c4), a medical facility (c5), and a vehicle (c6). Labeling the whole site 'residential_highrise' misrepresents the mix of targets actually described and contradicts c4, c5, and c6.

days.summary: On the night of October 3–4, 2026, Russian forces struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge with a jet-powered drone, damaging the roadway, trolleybus power lines and two vehicles, while falling debris caused fires and damage in Obolonskyi, Holosiivskyi, Desnianskyi and Dniprovskyi districts.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 1 and Site 2 both describe the exact same physical location and the same single strike: 'Northern Bridge' (c1: 'struck Kyiv's Northern Bridge... damaging the roadway and severing trolleybus power lines'; c2: 'Northern Bridge, two vehicles' / 'Одразу постраждали дві машини... Уламки на асфальті були'). Both claims are about the same jet-drone hit on the bridge reported within an hour of each other by different outlets, just emphasizing different effects (infrastructure damage vs. vehicle damage) of one impact. Splitting them into two separate sites double-counts a single strike on the Northern Bridge; they should be merged into one site covering both the roadway/power-line damage and the two damaged vehicles.

days.summary: On the night/morning of 5-6 October 2026, Russian strikes on Kyiv damaged a bridge roadway in Desnianskyi district, set vehicles on fire in a residential courtyard in Pecherskyi district, and caused a minor roof fire at an educational institution in Obolonskyi district.

days.summary: On the night and day of October 7, 2026, Russian strikes on Kyiv hit warehouses, a film studio, residential and administrative buildings, and vehicles across multiple districts, causing fires, partial destruction, injuries, and at least one death.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 7 merges at least two (arguably three) distinct physical incidents in Solomianskyi district into one site. Claims c8/c14/c16/c18/c28 all describe a '5-поверхового житлового будинку' (5-storey residential building) with fire on floors 1-3. Claims c9/c10/c17 describe a completely different object, explicitly flagged by the sources as a second location: c9 says 'Також у Соломʼянському районі загорівся приватний будинок' (ALSO a private house caught fire) and c17 repeats 'Також ... загорівся приватний будинок' — the word 'також' (also) marks this as a separate address from the 5-storey building. A private house ('приватний будинок', target residential_house) is a different kind of building than a 5-storey apartment block (target residential_highrise), so these cannot be the same site. The site's single target field 'residential_highrise' and weapon 'drone' therefore misrepresent the private-house claims, which never mention a drone and are target residential_house. This should be split into (at least) a 5-storey-building site and a private-house site.

c11 (KCMA, 17:15, Solom'yanskyi, open_area): 'Також, за іншою адресою, уламки впали на відкритій території. Одна людина отримала травми' (also, at another address, debris fell on open ground, one person injured). c32 (KCMA next-day summary, 08:30, Solom'yanskyi, target 'other'): 'За іншою адресою внаслідок падіння уламків БПЛА травмовано одну людину' (at another address, drone debris injured one person). Both describe the exact same distinguishing details — 'another address' in Solom'yanskyi, debris, exactly one person injured — matching the day-after-summary pattern used elsewhere in this attack (e.g. c28/c29/c30/c31 each restate the previous day's incidents). c32 should be merged with c11 into Site 8, not placed inside Site 7 with the residential-building/private-house claims.

c12 (KCMA, 17:22, Дніпровський, open_area): 'У Дніпровському районі уламки впали на відкритій території' (debris fell on open ground). c13 (Klitschko, 17:22, Дніпровський, education): 'У Дніпровському районі падіння уламків неподалік навчального закладу' (debris fall near an educational institution). These are posted by two different sources at the identical minute, same district, with no 'at another address' qualifier distinguishing a second incident (unlike e.g. c5/c11/c32 which explicitly say 'за іншою адресою' when a second site exists in the same district). This strongly suggests both describe the same single debris-fall event near a school, just worded with different specificity by KCMA vs. the Mayor — analogous to other same-incident duplicates in this dataset that were correctly merged (e.g. c3+c4, c19+c20). Kept as two separate sites, this risks double-counting one strike.

days.summary: On 8 October 2026, Russian drone strikes hit Kyiv's Solomianskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, and Holosiivskyi districts, with a direct hit and fire at a four-storey commercial building causing deaths and injuries, and debris falling in open areas including near parked vehicles that caught fire.

On the night of 9–10 October 2026, Russian drone and missile strikes damaged residential houses, a school, a heat pipeline, and a shop building across several districts of Kyiv, with a separate vehicle fire near a business center in Dniprovskyi district.

days.summary: On the night and day of 10 October 2026, drone and missile debris struck multiple districts of Kyiv — Podilskyi, Dniprovskyi, Solomianskyi, Obolonskyi, Shevchenkivskyi (reported as Sviatoshynskyi in two posts), Holosiivskyi and Darnytskyi — damaging a restaurant, residential buildings, an office building, a school stadium, vehicles and open ground, with a residential fire on Arkhitektora Verbytskoho Street and four people injured at the restaurant.

audit_examples.explanation: Claim c18 has target "open_area" ("У Дарницькому районі падіння уламків БпЛА на відкритій території. Пошкоджені декілька авто" — the debris fell on open ground, and vehicles were only incidentally damaged). The site's target field was changed to "vehicle", which is not what the claim states and misrepresents the nature of the impact site as a vehicle-target strike rather than an open-area debris fall.

Site 6's summary says 'Missile or drone debris fell...' but no claim in the site mentions a drone. c6 explicitly says the debris was from a missile ('уламки ракети впали в дворі житлового будинку'), while c9 and c11 give no weapon at all ('уламки впали в дворі житлового будинку' / weapon 'unknown'). The site's own weapon field is 'missile', so 'or drone' in the summary is invented and contradicts both the claims and the site's own weapon field.

Site 8 is labeled district 'Шевченківський', but both underlying claims explicitly name a different district in their quotes: c14 says 'У Святошинському районі уламки БпЛА впали на відкритій території шкільного стадіону' and c15 says 'У Святошинському районі уламки впали на відкритій території навчально закладу'. Neither quote mentions Шевченківський; the assigned district contradicts the text of both claims.

The summary states 'the district field is recorded as Shevchenkivskyi based on posting pattern' - this reasoning about 'posting pattern' appears nowhere in c14 or c15 and is not attributable to any source; it is invented justification for the district assignment rather than something any claim says.

days.summary: On the night/day of 11 October 2026, drone debris fell in two separate districts of Kyiv, damaging a car in Darnytskyi district and landing in a green zone near an apartment building in Holosiivskyi district.

On the night of 2026-10-12 into the morning of 2026-10-13, Russian drone and missile strikes hit Kyiv's Darnytskyi, Solomianskyi, Pecherskyi, Dniprovskyi and Desnianskyi districts, damaging private houses, a residential high-rise, a warehouse and transport infrastructure, with falling debris and fires reported in several locations.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 1 contains c12 (KCMA, 2026-10-13 07:16, Дарницький, 'уламки впали на територію приватного житлового будинку') and Site 8 is built solely from c13 (Mayor, 2026-10-13 08:00, Дарницький, 'уламки БпЛА пошкодили двоповерховий приватний житловий будинок та огорожу подвірʼя'). These two reports are 44 minutes apart, same district, same target type (residential_house), same general description (drone/unknown debris damaging a private house), with KCMA giving the brief first report and the Mayor giving the more detailed follow-up — the same pattern seen elsewhere in this dataset for a single incident (e.g. c1+c3, c9+c10). These are almost certainly the same strike site and should be one site, not split across Site 1 and Site 8; as separated now, the attack is double-counted.

c6 (SES, 16:15) states 'стались пожежі у одноповерховому та двоповерховому приватних житлових будинках' — fires broke out in a one-storey house AND a two-storey house, i.e. two distinct buildings. c1/c3 describe only one private house (no storey count given) catching fire from drone debris. The site folds c6 wholesale into the same single 'site' as c1/c3 and presents it (title: 'a private house', target: residential_house singular) as one location, but c6's second building (the two-storey house) is a separate physical structure with no address link to the house in c1/c3. The site therefore conflates at least two different houses into one entry instead of flagging that the SES report covers an additional, unidentified location.

days.summary: Overnight into the morning of October 13–14, 2026, Russia struck Kyiv with a combination of ballistic missiles and Shahed-type drones, hitting residential buildings in Desnianskyi and Darnytskyi districts, a thermal power plant, office and warehouse buildings, and open areas across at least six districts, causing fires, casualties and fatalities.

audit_examples.explanation: c3 (Kyiv Post, posted 2026-10-13 09:54) reports 'Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported strikes on transport infrastructure and a four-story warehouse', weapon 'ballistic', no district given. c21 (State Emergency Service, posted 2026-10-14 00:23 — almost 15 hours later) says 'За іншою адресою ворожий обстріл спричинив пожежу складської будівлі', with weapon 'unknown', and is explicitly introduced as being at 'іншою адресою' (another address) relative to the preceding item in that SES bulletin (the Desnianskyi 9-storey building strike, c20). There is no shared district, address, time proximity, or weapon between c3 and c21 — c3 is a daytime report naming a ballistic weapon, c21 is a late-night report from an entirely separate SES bulletin about the overnight missile barrage. The site's own summary admits the link is only 'likely the same strike', i.e. a guess rather than supported fact. c21 should not be merged with c3; it needs its own site (or to be checked against the other claims from the same 00:23 SES bulletin), not forced into the daytime warehouse report.

c15 (State Emergency Service, posted 20:50, Солом'янський) reports a direct hit causing fire in a 'non-residential building' ('внаслідок влучання у нежитлову будівлю виникло загоряння'). c14 (Suspilne Kyiv, posted 21:03, only 13 minutes later, same district) reports 'БпЛА влучив в офісну будівлю' — a drone hit on an office building, which is itself a type of non-residential building, with matching effects (direct hit, fire/blast damage). These two claims, posted minutes apart in the same district with matching damage type, are much better evidence of describing the same strike than the roughly 3.5–4-hour-earlier reports c11 (Klitschko, 17:22) and c13 (Kyiv Post, 17:27), which the matcher grouped together with c14 into site 8. It is more likely that c14 belongs with c15 as a second, later office/non-residential building strike in Солом'янський, and that the matcher mistakenly kept c14 with the 17:22 reports instead of merging it with the near-simultaneous c15 report, leaving site 9 (c15 alone) as an under-merged duplicate of part of site 8.

Site 6 (c7+c8) and Site 7 (c9) are both located in Солом'янський district and describe debris/drone impact in open ground at or next to a park. c7 (12:20): 'уламки БпЛА впали та горять на відкритій території біля одного з парків'. c8 (12:43): 'уламки впали на відкритій території внаслідок чого пошкоджено кав'ярню та постраждало двоє людей' — two people injured. c9 (13:44): 'У парку «Орлятко» в Солом'янському районі уламки дрона травмували двох жінок віком 35 та 40 років' — two women injured. The casualty count matches exactly (двоє людей = двох жінок), the district matches, the cause (debris/drone) matches, and the reports arrive in a tight 84-minute sequence with increasing detail (generic park area -> café hit, 2 injured -> named park 'Orliatko', ages of the 2 injured given). This strongly indicates one single strike site progressively detailed by three sources, not two separate sites. Site 7 should be merged into Site 6.

Site 11 merges c16 (22:42), c20 (00:23) and c23 (00:34), all describing a direct hit with fire on a '9-storey residential building' in Деснянський district, culminating in 1 killed/8 injured. Site 18 separately holds c26 (07:32, same source: State Emergency Service, Kyiv), which states: 'на місці ворожого удару по багатоповерхівці у Деснянському районі вогнеборці ліквідували пожежу на площі 400 кв. м' — i.e. firefighters finally extinguished the fire at the strike site on a multi-storey building in the SAME district. This is the same pattern the matcher correctly recognized for other locations in the same 07:32 SES bulletin: the Дарницький stadium lawn fire (c19/c22/c28) and the Голосіївський building (c25/c30) were each merged across multiple timestamps as follow-up/extinguished reports of the same site. c26 fits the identical pattern (same district, same building category 'residential_highrise', fire status progressing from ongoing to extinguished) and should be merged into Site 11 rather than left as a separate Site 18, otherwise the same strike is counted twice.

c5 only says 'place': '3-storey non-residential building' and quotes 'зруйнована триповерхова нежитлова будівля' — it never identifies the building as industrial. Site 4 sets target to 'industrial', an invented categorization with no support in the claim. Elsewhere the matcher correctly tagged equally generic 'non-residential building' claims (c25, c27, c29, c30) as target 'other'; c5 should be tagged the same way instead of 'industrial'.

days.summary: On 14 October 2026, a Russian ballistic missile struck a 9-storey residential building in Kyiv's Desnianskyi district, while separately an electric car exploded in Pecherskyi district, injuring its driver.

On the night and day of 15 October 2026, Russian drone strikes hit Pechersk district twice (a car fire between two residential buildings, and a separate drone impact damaging a five-storey building, a school and a swimming pool), a warehouse in Sviatoshynskyi district was struck twice, and fires broke out at a private house in Shevchenkivskyi district and an outbuilding in Solomianskyi district.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 1 appears to fuse two different physical incidents in Pechersk into one. One strand describes a car fire between two 3-storey buildings: c3 'фасади двох триповерхових житлових будинків поруч. Палає автівка в дворі' and c4 'вогнеборці ліквідували пожежу автомобіля ... П'ятеро людей постраждали' (5 injured, tied specifically to the car fire). The other strand describes a drone landing near a 5-storey building that also damaged a school and pool: c2 'БпЛА впав на відкритій території біля 5-поверхового житлового будинку', c5 '7 постраждалих внаслідок падіння ворожого БпЛА між житловими будинками', and c6 'The blast damaged a five-story building, a school, and a local swimming pool' (6 injured, 3 hospitalized). A 5-storey building and 'two 3-storey buildings' cannot be the same structure, the school/pool damage is never linked to the car-fire buildings, and the injury tallies run 5 (car fire) then 7 then 6 (drone/5-storey branch) rather than one consistent count for a single site. This looks like two separate impact points in the same district being merged into one site, which risks under-counting distinct strikes.

The summary states 'casualty counts rising from 5 to 7 injured', but the claims given are 5 (c4), 7 (c5) and then 6 with 3 hospitalized (c6, posted after c5 at 16:25). The summary silently drops the final '6 injured, 3 hospitalized' figure and wrongly implies a monotonic rise capping at 7, which is not what the sourced claims say.

Claims c2, c5, c6 describe a drone impact near a 5-storey residential building in Pechersk that also damaged a school and swimming pool, with casualty counts of 0 (c2), 7 injured (c5), and 6 injured/3 hospitalized (c6: 'The blast damaged a five-story building, a school, and a local swimming pool'). None of these three claims appear in Site 1 or any other site produced by the matcher.

Claims c7 and c8 describe fire/direct hits on a warehouse building in Святошинський district ('загоряння в складській будівлі' and 'Повторне влучання в складську будівлю'). They are entirely absent from the site list.

Claims c9 and c10 describe a fire at a private residential house (and outbuilding) in Шевченківський district ('загоряння приватного житлового будинку' and 'пожежа господарської нежитлової будівлі та приватного житлового будинку'). They are missing from every site.
Claim c11 describes an outbuilding fire in Солом'янський district ('горіла господарча будівля'), a different district from any site produced. It is missing from every site.

days.summary: On the night of 16 October 2026, Russian strikes caused fires at a non-residential building and a private house in Shevchenkivskyi district and at a non-residential (outbuilding) structure in Solomianskyi district.

Overnight on 18–19 October 2026, Russian strikes hit Kyiv's Desnianskyi, Dniprovskyi, and Solomianskyi districts, damaging a medical center, educational and sports facilities, a metro station, a 25-storey residential building (with debris, direct hits, a fire in its ground-floor clinic, and injuries), a non-residential building/shopping center, and several other non-residential structures and parked vehicles.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 6 and Site 8 both describe the same 25-storey residential building in Solomianskyi district, not two different buildings. Site 6's claims describe debris/direct hit to the building (c4/c6: "уламків в перший поверх 25-поверхового житлового будинку"; c9: "влучання в 25-поверховий житловий будинок"; c12: injuries from missile debris at this building). Site 8's claim c15, from the State Emergency Service at the same overnight timeframe, says "сталось загоряння у приміщені медичного закладу на третьому поверсі 25-поверхового житлового будинку" — a fire in a clinic on the 3rd floor of a 25-storey residential building in the same district. No address differentiates this from the building in Site 6, and it is far more likely the SES report is describing a secondary effect (fire reaching the 3rd-floor clinic) of the same strike on the same high-rise than a second, separate 25-storey residential building being hit in Solomianskyi that night. These should be one site, with the medical facility noted as an affected part of the building.

Site 7's claims (c5, c7, c10) all describe a second impact point in Solomianskyi district at "іншою адресою" from the residential high-rise, generically called a "non-residential building" ("нежитлову будівлю"/"нежитловий будинок") by three sources reporting within minutes of each other (03:30–03:37). None of these three simultaneous reports mention a third location in the district. Site 9's claim c19, reported later (08:50) by the military administration, specifies "пошкоджено скління навколишніх будинків та будівлю торгового центру" — damage to a shopping center building and nearby windows, also in Solomianskyi. Given the pattern elsewhere in this dataset (e.g. the Dniprovskyi education claims, where later reports add specificity such as "спортивний заклад" to an initially generic "заклади освіти"), c19 most likely supplies the specific identity (a shopping center) of the same non-residential building referenced generically in c5/c7/c10, rather than describing an unrelated third site. Treating them as separate sites risks double-counting one strike location.

Site 3 is built around education-facility reports (c3, c16, c17), but c18 explicitly says 'також зафіксовано падіння уламків на нежитлову забудову' ('ALSO recorded debris falling onto non-residential development') — the word 'також' signals this is a separate location from the schools/sports facility just mentioned in the same report. Folding it into the education site mislabels a non-residential-building/territory incident as part of the education-facility strike. This claim's wording ('нежитлову забудову') closely mirrors c8 in site 4 ('територію нежитлової забудови'), both from the same district, suggesting c18 should instead be merged with site 4 rather than site 3.

Site 5's summary says the building 'sustained a direct hit on its first floor,' but no single claim states this combination. c4 and c6 describe debris ('уламків') hitting the first floor, not a direct hit; c9 separately reports a direct hit ('влучання') on the building with no floor specified. The summary invents a detail (direct hit specifically on the first floor) that isn't in any source claim.

The site's 'address' field is set to 'ТРЦ' (an abbreviation for shopping/trade center), but none of the claims c5, c7, c10, or c19 give an actual address — they say 'за іншою адресою' (at another address, unspecified) or simply name the facility type. Putting a facility-type label into the address field misrepresents the claims as containing address information they don't have.

days.summary: On the night of 19 October 2026, Russian strikes on Kyiv damaged a medical diagnostic center, the Chernihivska metro station and surrounding area, the Shalet ice arena, a Datagroup data center, the Cosmo Multimall shopping centre, and the Book Chamber of Ukraine.

On the night and day of 20–21 October 2026, Kyiv endured a prolonged drone attack hitting medical facilities, academic and bank buildings, a residential high-rise, an energy facility, transport infrastructure, warehouses, garages and open areas across multiple districts, with casualties reported at a Solomianskyi medical facility and a Holosiivskyi medical facility.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 2 merges two different medical-facility incidents in two different districts. c2 ("У Солом'янському районі уламки впали на будівлю медичного закладу") and c3 ("У Соломʼянському районі влучання БпЛА в верхній поверх будівлю медзакладу... Є часткове руйнування даху") are explicitly in Солом'янський district. c6 ("у Голосіївському районі уламки впали на будівлю медичного закладу") and c8 ("Двоє постраждалих в Голосіївському районі внаслідок влучання уламків у будівлю медичного закладу") are explicitly in Голосіївський district. These are two separate buildings in two separate districts, not one site. The site's own summary betrays the problem by saying 'Holosiivskyi/Solomiansky district' and its district field is set only to 'Голосіївський', which contradicts c2/c3.

The Solomianskyi medical-facility claims wrongly placed in Site 2 (c2: debris at 13:38; c3: direct hit on upper floor/roof at 13:53, both district Солом'янський) are the same evolving incident later identified by name in Site 8: c11 (Kyiv Post, 17:23) names it 'Institute of Cardiology, operating room'; c16 (Suspilne, 18:05) names it 'Strazheska Institute building'; c19 (SES, 20:13) confirms 'health facility building in Solomianskyi' with blast damage. All five claims describe one place (the Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology in Солом'янський) at increasing levels of detail over the day and should be one site. Notably, Site 8's own summary already states 'the city administration ... also reported blast damage to a health facility building in the same district', but no Kyiv City Military Administration claim is actually present in Site 8's claim list (c2 is the city-administration claim, and it was misplaced into Site 2 instead), confirming the merge was missed.

These five claims all come from the same Suspilne Kyiv report filed in two parts (18:05 and 18:44) about damage in Голосіївський district and almost certainly describe one strike location with several affected buildings, but the matcher split them into four separate sites. c13 (18:05, 'уламки безпілотника влучили у будівлю НАН') is elaborated 39 minutes later by the same source in c17 (18:44, 'Інституту водних проблем і меліорації НАН України в Києві') — i.e. the generic 'NAN building' is the named Institute of Water Problems and Melioration. Likewise c14 (18:05, PrivatBank/Oschadbank buildings) and c15 (18:05, three residential houses) are recapped together in the same source's follow-up c18 (18:44: 'Також пошкоджені будівлі відділень банків, три житлові будинки та припарковані поруч автомобілі'), which explicitly re-lists banks + three houses + cars as part of the same ongoing account used to build c17/c18. The matcher correctly merged c15+c18 into Site 12, but left c13, c14 and c17 as three additional separate sites for what is the same strike/location cluster, double- and triple-counting one event.

Site 6 (c7) and Site 7 (c9) both describe debris/impact on open ground in the same district (Деснянський), only 17 minutes apart (16:04 and 16:21), with c7 from KCMA ('уламки впали на відкритій території') and c9 from the Mayor adding more detail ('влучання БпЛА на відкритій території біля зеленої зони'). This is the same KCMA-then-Mayor escalating-detail reporting pattern (brief initial report, then a fuller follow-up with added specifics) that the matcher itself used to justify merging Site 2 (c2 KCMA 13:38 + c3 Mayor 13:53, 15-minute gap) and Site 5 (c6 KCMA 15:25 + c8 Mayor 16:08, 43-minute gap). There is no distinguishing location detail in c9 that contradicts c7 ('near a green zone' is compatible with 'open ground'), so treating c7/c9 as two separate impact sites likely double-counts a single strike.

days.summary: On the night of 21–22 October 2026, Russian ballistic and drone strikes hit at least nine distinct sites across Kyiv — residential buildings in Svyatoshynskyi, private houses, a car service station and a gas station in Dniprovskyi, metro infrastructure on the Pivdenny Bridge in Darnytskyi, medical facilities and a monastery in Pecherskyi, a restaurant complex in Svyatoshynskyi, and non-residential buildings in Obolonskyi and Holosiivskyi — killing at least two people and injuring dozens.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 8 (c17, c27) reports a generic 'transportation infrastructure facility' / 'транспортну інфраструктуру' hit in Дарницький district, with no address given. Site 9 (c19, c32) reports metro infrastructure damaged specifically 'на Південному мосту' (Pivdenny/Southern Bridge). The Pivdenny Bridge, which carries the Kyiv metro, sits on the Darnytskyi side of the river. c17 and c19 are both from Mayor Klitschko, posted the same night (00:05 and 05:48), with c19 reading like the specific follow-up/clarification of the vague c17 report; c27 (SES, 08:05, 'Дарницький район. Пошкоджено транспортну інфраструктуру') likewise looks like the generic district-level confirmation of the same metro-bridge damage reported specifically by c32 (Ukrainska Pravda, 08:08, 'на Південному мосту — інфраструктура метро'). These look like the same physical object (the Pivdenny Bridge/metro infrastructure) described at different levels of specificity rather than two separate strike locations, so treating them as two sites likely double-counts one impact.

Site 3 is built from c7 (KCMA, 22:31, generic 'пошкоджено приватні житлові будинки' — plural, no address) and c26 (SES, next-morning overview: 'Пошкоджено будинки й автомобілі, горіли житлові та нежитлові будівлі' for the whole Дніпровський district). These are both district-wide summary statements, not a distinct address. Meanwhile sites 6 ('private residential house hit', c10+c14 — direct hit) and 7 ('debris damaged another residential house', c11+c15 — debris) already describe the specific private houses that were hit in Дніпровський that night (reported in more detail by Klitschko/hromadske at 22:49/23:21). c7's early, vague 'residential houses damaged' line is almost certainly the preliminary version of exactly these same two houses, not a third separate location. Giving it its own 'Site 3' alongside sites 6 and 7 risks presenting the same one or two houses as three separate impact points, double-counting the damage.

Site 7 is labeled weapon "unknown", but a majority of its own claims specify the weapon: c20 ("У Печерському районі пошкоджена будівля станції швидкої допомоги", weapon ballistic), c21 ("також пошкоджень зазнали шість автомобілів швидкої", weapon ballistic) and c30 ("Пошкоджено будівлі, автомобілі швидкої допомоги та монастир...", weapon ballistic) all report ballistic. Only c18 and c25 leave weapon unspecified ("unknown"). This is inconsistent with how the matcher handled identical situations elsewhere: in Sites 2, 3, 4 and 5, a mix of "unknown" and "ballistic" claims was resolved to "ballistic" rather than "unknown". Site 7 should likewise be "ballistic".

The Site 7 summary states "eight people were injured, including three children" as if this casualty figure belongs specifically to the medical facility/ambulance station damage described in the site. But the only source for this number, c30, actually attributes it to a combined district report: "Пошкоджено будівлі, автомобілі швидкої допомоги та монастир. Постраждали восьмеро людей, серед них троє дітей" — i.e. buildings, ambulances AND the Svyato-Vvedenskyi Monastery together (the monastery is a separate site, Site 9, which carries no casualty figure of its own). Presenting the 8-injured/3-children number as specific to the medical/ambulance incident is not supported by the claim, which ties it to a broader set of damage including the monastery.

days.summary: On the night/morning of 22 October 2026, Russian ballistic missile strikes hit multiple districts of Kyiv, damaging residential houses, non-residential buildings, a medical facility, a monastery, two retail parks, metro infrastructure and a museum, with fires reported at several sites.

audit_examples.explanation: Both claims come from the same KCMA bulletin, same district (Дніпровський), same timestamp, and c2's quote begins with 'Також пошкоджено нежитлову забудову' (also damaged is a non-residential building) — i.e. it is presented as additional damage at the SAME spot, not a new location. Contrast this with the Печерський entries in the same bulletin (c7 vs c8), where the second item explicitly says 'За іншою адресою' (at another address) to signal a distinct site. Because c2 lacks that explicit 'different address' marker, it most likely describes the same impact point as c1 (residential houses plus an adjacent non-residential building), the same way c4 combines 'restaurant and non-residential building' as one site. Splitting c1 and c2 into Site 1 and Site 2 likely double-counts a single strike.

Site 5 (Epicentr hypermarket + cargo post office, Оболонський) and Site 10 (JYSK store near Pochaina metro + Pochaina retail park) plausibly describe the same retail complex rather than two separate strikes. c15 says the blast damaged 'обидва торгові блоки' (both retail blocks) of the Pochaina retail park, 'один із них частково зруйнований' (one of them partially destroyed) — this matches the pattern of a multi-tenant retail park where an Epicentr hypermarket (c12, c9 — ~1000 sq m destroyed by fire) and a JYSK store (c14 — completely burned) occupy the two separate blocks, with a cargo post office (c10) nearby. None of c14/c15 give a district or address that rules out Оболонський/Pochaina proximity, and no claim distinguishes this as a second, separate strike location. As written, the grouping risks reporting one strike on a single retail park as two different impact sites.

Site 8 sets weapon to 'missile', but two of the three underlying claims explicitly classify the weapon as 'ballistic' (c8: "weapon": "ballistic"; c13: "weapon": "ballistic"). Only c17 uses the generic term 'missile' ("Уламки ракети посікли дах монастиря"). The site's weapon field overrides the majority classification from the claims without justification, contradicting c8 and c13.

days.summary: On the night of 2026-10-23, Kyiv city administration reports referenced cumulative damage from the October 19 and October 21 attacks (not this attack day), while a confirmed strike on this date damaged a private residential house in the Obolonskyi district, injuring two people.

audit_examples.explanation: The claims in these two sites explicitly describe strikes on two different calendar dates, not a single attack day. c1's quote says the damage (1 killed, 8 injured, metro station hit) resulted from 'ворожої атаки 19 жовтня' (the enemy attack of October 19), while c2's quote says its damage (6 injured, debris near a gas station) resulted from 'російського обстрілу 21 жовтня' (the Russian shelling of October 21). Since this batch is supposed to represent impact sites for one attack day, at least one of these sites (c1 or c2) belongs to a different day's attack than the one being documented here and should not be included alongside the other.

days.summary: Overnight into 24 October, Kyiv was hit by drone attacks and other strikes, damaging a private house in Obolonskyi district, parked vehicles in Shevchenkivskyi district, and causing debris to fall into a forest strip in Desnianskyi district.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 2 sets target to 'vehicle', but claim c2 explicitly has target field 'open_area' (place: 'parking area with vehicles'). The incident is drone debris falling on an open parking lot that happened to damage cars, not an attack on a vehicle target. The site's target field contradicts the claim's own target classification.

The summary adds an invented justification not present in the claim: 'The strike target is classified as open area, since the debris fell on open ground and incidentally damaged parked cars rather than striking a vehicle directly.' The source quote only says debris fell on an open parking area and damaged cars without fire ('Пошкоджені авто, без загоряння') — it contains no explanation or reasoning about why the target is classified as open_area versus a vehicle strike. This reasoning is fabricated by the summary writer, not drawn from the claim.

days.summary: On the night of 25 October 2026, drone debris and strikes caused fires and debris falls in open areas of Kyiv's Dniprovskyi and Desnianskyi districts, with no casualties or infrastructure damage reported.

On the night of 26-27 October 2026, Russian forces struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles and other weapons, hitting a university campus area near Lisova metro station in Desnianskyi district (damaging the metro station, a car, an ambulance, dormitories, a school and nearby residential buildings), along with a medical facility, a non-residential building, and scattered damage to residential, administrative, warehouse and transport infrastructure across several districts, including the South Bridge.

audit_examples.explanation: Sites 1, 2, 3 and 4 are split pieces of one single ballistic strike on the Lisova metro / Kyoto park university campus area in Деснянський district, not four separate places. c12 (in site 4) explicitly states the missile hit 'по території одного з університетів і поруч із ним – фактично по кампусу, по парку «Кіото», по території поруч зі станцією метро, житловими будинками' — i.e. the metro-station area (site 1) is described as part of the same campus strike footprint as the dormitory (site 4). c14 (placed in site 1) says in one sentence that there are 'руйнування біля супермаркету "Ашан"', that 'Пошкоджена станція метро "Лісова"', AND 'гуртожиток торговельно-економічного університету' — directly tying the metro station to the university dormitory that is grouped in site 4. c21 (placed in site 4) reports together that 'пошкоджені будівля студентського гуртожитку та автівка, що стояла поруч зі станцією метро' — meaning the exact same 'car near the metro' fact that sites 1 (c1 'Палає авто' near metro Lisova) and 3 (c17 'влучання в легковий автомобіль поблизу однієї зі станцій метро') describe is already embedded inside site 4's own claim. So one car near the metro is currently counted across three different sites (1, 3, 4). The ambulance crew (site 2: c3, c7, c9) is reported in the same breath as the metro-station hit in both source streams — Suspilne's c8 ('влучання біля однієї зі станцій метро') is immediately followed by c9 ('Також під обстріл потрапила бригада медиків швидкої...'), and Klitschko's c1/c2 metro report at 22:03 is immediately followed by c3 at the same 22:03 timestamp — indicating the ambulance was hit in the same strike's immediate vicinity, not a separate location. All four sites should be merged into one site covering the metro station, car, ambulance, dormitory, campus/park, nearby residential buildings and school, otherwise this single strike is double- or quadruple-counted.

Site 6 (c6) and Site 7 (c18) are very likely the same incident reported at two different times, not two separate strikes. c6 (Klitschko, 22:29) says 'влучання в будівлю на території нежитлової забудови... біля одного з супермаркетів поруч є загиблий' (a non-residential building hit, one fatality nearby, preliminary). c18 (SES, 23:50) says 'часткове руйнування триповерхової нежитлової будівлі від покрівлі до підвалу... виявлено одну загиблу людину' (partial destruction of a three-storey non-residential building, one body found). Both are in Дніпровський district, both describe a non-residential building, and both report exactly one fatality, with no other non-residential-building incident reported for Dniprovskyi that night. This reads as the preliminary report (c6) being superseded/detailed by the later official SES report (c18) about the same building, and should be one site, not two.

Site 3's target field is set to 'warehouse' (matching c18's own tag), but the other claim merged into this site, c6, explicitly self-tags its target as 'commercial', not 'warehouse'. c6's quote is 'У Дніпровському районі також влучання в будівлю на території нежитлової забудови. days.summary: On the night of 29–30 October 2026, Russian strikes hit Kyiv's Dniprovskyi, Darnytskyi, Holosiivskyi and Obolonskyi districts, damaging residential buildings, warehouses, a shop, a gas station and causing a road collapse, with multiple fires reported.

audit_examples.explanation: c7 (Klitschko, 23:29) is explicitly the third in a sequence of distinct addresses the Mayor reported ('за іншою адресою' → c5, 'на іншій локації' → c6, 'іще за однією адресою' → c7), and its own target field is 'residential_highrise'. c11 (State Emergency Service, next morning 07:16) has target 'residential_house' — a different building category — and its own quote says the damage it describes occurred 'на двох локаціях' (at two locations), meaning c11 already bundles two separate sites of its own. None of the underlying claims (c7, c11) say anything about prior audit or auditor feedback - this is the first audit pass of this grouping, so no such feedback exists in the claim data. These phrases insert an unsupported, fabricated justification into the summary that is not derived from any source claim and reads as an attempt to preempt scrutiny of the grouping decision rather than describe the incident.

audit_examples.explanation: c2 (KCMA, 12:14) reports 'У Деснянському районі внаслідок падіння БпЛА виникло загоряння офісної будівлі' and c6 (SES, 13:05) reports 'Деснянський район: виникло загоряння покрівлі 3-поверхової будівлі.' These are the only two claims about Desnianskyi district that day, posted about an hour apart by the exact same pair of agencies (KCMA then SES) that, for Holosiivskyi district, reported the same single incident via c3 and c5 — which the matcher correctly merged into Site 4. There is no evidence of a second, distinct incident in Desnianskyi; c6's 'roof of a 3-storey building' almost certainly refers to the same office building fire named in c2, just described with more structural detail. Sites 2 and 3 should be one site.

Site 7 (c8, KCMA 15:13: 'В Оболонському районі уламки впали на відкритій території') and Site 10 (c11 Klitschko 15:29: 'В Оболонському районі горять уламки на проїжджій частині дороги', plus c15 Suspilne and c33 SES) describe the same open-ground/roadway debris event in Obolonskyi district, just reported with increasing specificity by different sources minutes to hours apart (KCMA's generic 'open territory' at 15:13 is echoed/clarified as 'roadway' by the mayor 16 minutes later, then Suspilne and SES). No other Obolonskyi debris incident exists in the claim set for this time window, so c8 should be folded into Site 10 rather than left as a standalone Site 7.

Site 32 contains only c63, a Ukrainska Pravda report posted the next morning (2026-11-20 08:34): 'російський дрон завдав пошкоджень посольству країни в Києві' about the 'Embassy of the Netherlands.' Site 12 already documents a drone strike on the building behind the Dutch Embassy and an impact in the embassy's own courtyard (c19, c26, c37), reported the evening before by the same categories of sources (Ukrainska Pravda/hromadske/Kyiv Post). c63 names the same embassy and same weapon (drone) with no new address, time, or detail suggesting a second, distinct strike — it reads as a later recap of the same event. Keeping it as a separate Site 32 double-counts the Dutch Embassy strike.

Site 26 ('Fire at non-residential building in Podilskyi district') is built around c47/c55 ('У Подільському районі загоряння будівлі в нежитловій забудові' — a building fire), but the matcher also placed c61 there, which actually says 'В Подільському та Дарницькому районах внаслідок ворожої атаки постраждала транспортно-логістична інфраструктура' — damage to transport-logistics infrastructure, not a building fire. The identically-worded Darnytskyi half of this same report, c62, was correctly placed with the Darnytskyi bridge site (Site 29). For consistency, c61 should instead be grouped with the Podilskyi bridge site (Site 28, Podilsko-Voskresenskyi bridge crossing), since that bridge is the transport-logistics infrastructure item in Podilskyi — it does not belong with Site 26's warehouse/building fire.

These three sites are almost certainly the same single incident (debris landing in the open territory by St. Volodymyr's Cathedral, damaging parked cars, the cathedral's windows, and a nearby embassy's windows), not three separate strikes. c24 (Kyiv Post, 17:15) explicitly bundles two of the 'separate' sites into one sentence: "Falling Russian drone debris in Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi district damaged over 10 vehicles and shattered windows at St. Volodymyr's Cathedral" — i.e. the exact facts split between Site 15 (vehicles) and Site 16 (cathedral). Even stronger, c34 (SES, 17:47), which the matcher placed only in Site 16, describes a single event in one sentence covering all three sites: "уламки впали на відкритій території Володимирського кафедрального собору: пошкоджені орієнтовно 12 легкових авто [Site 15], скління вікон культової споруди [Site 16], а також скління будівлі поруч розташованого посольства [Site 17] та авто." Also c21, c22 and c23 were all posted by the mayor at the identical timestamp 17:06, consistent with one thread about one location. Splitting this into Sites 15/16/17 double- (triple-)counts a single strike.

Site 33 merges c59 and c60 into one site with a single district value "Оболонський", but the source quote underlying both claims explicitly names two different districts as separate locations: "В Оболонському та Голосіївському районах внаслідок ворожої атаки постраждала нежитлова забудова." Обоlonskyi and Holosiivskyi are different parts of the city, so this is not one physical place; forcing them into one site and labeling it only "Оболонський" loses the Holosiivskyi damage reported in c60.

Site 6's weapon field is "unknown", but one of its own merged claims, c33, explicitly states the weapon: "сталося падіння уламків ворожого безпілотника" (weapon: drone). The matcher applies the opposite, correct logic elsewhere — e.g. Site 14 merges c20 (weapon unknown) with c25 (weapon drone) and adopts "drone" — so Site 6 should likewise report weapon "drone" rather than "unknown".

days.summary: Falling debris and a ballistic strike caused fires and damage at several sites across Kyiv's Podilskyi, Holosiivskyi, and Solomianskyi districts, with the Pivdennyi Bridge also affected by damage amid the attack.

On the night/day of November 22–23, 2026, Russian drone strikes on Kyiv caused a vehicle fire in the Desnianskyi district and debris falls on a warehouse-type building in the Podilskyi district and on two separate educational facilities in the Sviatoshynskyi district; a reported incident in Bila Tserkva raion of Kyiv Oblast was excluded as it is outside Kyiv city.

audit_examples.explanation: The only claim in this site, c1, states the incident occurred 'У Білоцерківському районі' — Bila Tserkva raion, which is an administrative raion of Kyiv Oblast (centered on the separate city of Bila Tserkva), not a district of Kyiv city. The site's own summary even says 'in Bila Tserkva district', confirming this strike is outside the city of Kyiv and should not be included in this Kyiv-city attack-day dataset.

days.summary: On the night/evening of 23 November 2026, Russian drone strikes and falling debris caused fires and damage across Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi, Podilskyi, Pecherskyi, Holosiivskyi, and Sviatoshynskyi districts, hitting residential buildings, vehicles, and a critical infrastructure facility.

audit_examples.explanation: Site 5 (c5, c9: "попередньо, влучання БпЛА в житловий будинок" / "безпілотник упав на житловий будинок") gives no address, floor count, or any other detail that distinguishes it from the two already-identified drone-on-roof incidents in Site 6 (c12: explicitly a 6-storey building) and Site 7 (c19: explicitly a 5-storey building with a mansard fire). Klitschko and hromadske each posted only once about Podilskyi, with purely generic wording ('a residential building'), which is exactly what an early/undetailed report of one of those two already-confirmed buildings would look like, not necessarily a third location. As presented, Site 5 reads as a third separate residential-building drone strike in Podilskyi, which risks double- (or triple-) counting one of the two strikes already captured in Sites 6 and 7. There is no claim text that supports three distinct buildings being hit. Additionally, within Site 5 itself the target field is set to 'residential_highrise' even though claim c5's own target field is 'residential_house', a contradiction the site summary does not acknowledge.

Site 2 (c18, State Emergency Service) describes 'загоряння на парковці біля нежитлової споруди' (fire at a parking lot near a non-residential building) in Голосіївський district — the same district, same effect (cars/parking on fire from a strike), and the only Holosiivskyi incident reported all day. SES often avoids naming a 'critical infrastructure facility' explicitly for security reasons and instead calls it a 'non-residential building', which matches the facility described in c1/c7/c13/c15 ('обʼєкту критичної інфраструктури... спалахнули автівки'). The matcher itself admits in the summary 'it is unclear if this is the same site' but still kept it as a separate site instead of merging, risking double-counting one strike as two.

Site 3 contains only c2 ('палає автівка' - a car is burning, Mayor Klitschko, 15:22, Шевченківський, center of city), while Site 5 contains the fuller account of the same district/area from the same mayor only 31 minutes later (c4, 15:53: 'загоряння двох авто... пожежа на першому поверсі 5-поверхового житлового будинку'). This is the classic pattern of an initial brief report (one car) being followed by the same official's fuller update (two cars + building) about the same single incident in the same district center. Keeping c2 as its own site duplicates the Shevchenkivskyi building/car incident already captured in Site 5.

Site 4 contains only c3 (Kyiv City Military Administration, 15:30: 'у Печерсьому районі також виникло загоряння автомобіля внаслідок падіння уламків' — one car fire). Site 9 (c14, c17) is the later, more detailed account of the same Pecherskyi incident — a car fire that spread to a 5-storey residential building, eventually described as two cars (c17: 'загоряння двох автомобілів'). The summary of Site 4 even explicitly flags this uncertainty ('reported as a separate vehicle fire from the later residential building fire in the same district') rather than resolving it. As with Shevchenkivskyi, this looks like an early brief report of the same single Pecherskyi incident that was later elaborated, so treating it as a separate site likely double-counts the strike.

Site 6's target field is set to 'residential_house', but one of its own claims, c9, has target 'residential_highrise' ('У Подільському районі безпілотник упав на житловий будинок' — matching the multi-storey apartment buildings described elsewhere in Podil, c12 and c19). Both c5 and c9 only say generic 'житловий будинок' with no indication of a detached house; labeling the site 'residential_house' is unsupported and contradicts c9's own target classification.

flags: Site 3 contains only c2 ('палає автівка' - a car is burning, Mayor Klitschko, 15:22, Шевченківський, center of city), while Site 5 contains the fuller account of the same district/area from the same mayor only 31 minutes later (c4, 15:53: 'загоряння двох авто... пожежа на першому поверсі 5-поверхового житлового будинку'). This is the classic pattern of an initial brief report (one car) being followed by the same official's fuller update (two cars + building) about the same single incident in the same district center. Keeping c2 as its own site duplicates the Shevchenkivskyi building/car incident already captured in Site 5.

sites.title: Drone hit on residential building in Podilskyi district
sites.summary: A drone hit a residential building in Podilskyi district. Early reports from Klitschko and hromadske gave only generic details ('residential building') without an address or floor count, so this is likely an early/undetailed account of one of the two more specific drone strikes also reported in Podilskyi (a 6-storey building roof and a 5-storey building with a mansard fire) rather than a separate, third building; it is kept here because the claims themselves do not state which of the two it refers to.

Both c5 and c9 only say generic 'житловий будинок' with no indication of a detached house; labeling the site 'residential_house' is unsupported and contradicts c9's own target classification.

sources.quote: у Печерському районі внаслідок російського обстрілу сталося загоряння двох автомобілів з подальшим розповсюдженням на балкон житлової п'ятиповерхівки.

flags: Site 4 contains only c3 (Kyiv City Military Administration, 15:30: 'у Печерсьому районі також виникло загоряння автомобіля внаслідок падіння уламків' — one car fire). Site 9 (c14, c17) is the later, more detailed account of the same Pecherskyi incident — a car fire that spread to a 5-storey residential building, eventually described as two cars (c17: 'загоряння двох автомобілів'). sources.quote: У Голосіївському районі внаслідок ворожого удару сталось загоряння на парковці біля нежитлової споруди.

flags: Site 2 (c18, State Emergency Service) describes 'загоряння на парковці біля нежитлової споруди' (fire at a parking lot near a non-residential building) in Голосіївський district — the same district, same effect (cars/parking on fire from a strike), and the only Holosiivskyi incident reported all day.
